Kuvitus: astronautti loikkaa Kuun harmaa: Illustration: an astronaut leaps across the grey surface of the Moon, and his footprints show in the dust. The Earth, with oceans, continents and clouds, is visible in the black sky.
Kuvitus: sama reppu riippuu jousivaa'ass: Illustration: the same backpack hangs from a spring balance on Earth and on the Moon. On Earth the spring stretches far, on the Moon only one sixth as much, because the Moon pulls the backpack six times more weakly. The extensions are drawn to scale.
Voimamittari, periaatekuva, ei mittakaav: Force meter, schematic figure, not to scale. Two identical springs hang from a stand: an object of mass m hangs from the left-hand spring and two identical objects from the right-hand one. Double the weight stretches the spring double the distance. The weight G of each object is an arrow pointing down.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: jousen venymä x s: Graph to scale: extension x of a spring in centimetres as a function of force F, for F from 0 to 11 N. The measurement points 2.5 N and 1.0 cm, 5.0 N and 2.0 cm, and 10 N and 4.0 cm are on the same straight line through the origin; dashed lines show the values of the points on the axes.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: paino G newtonein: Graph to scale: weight G in newtons as a function of mass m, for m from 0 to 100 kg. Four straight lines through the origin, from steepest to gentlest: Jupiter (the line continues past the top edge of the figure), Earth (100 kg weighs 981 N), Mars (371 N) and the Moon (162 N).
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: erään jousen veny: Graph to scale: extension x of a spring in centimetres as a function of force F. Five measurement points without a drawn line: (2 N; 1 cm), (4 N; 2 cm), (6 N; 3 cm), (8 N; 4 cm) and (10 N; 5 cm). The grid spacing is 1 N and 1 cm.
